subject: Seller marketplace: GST apportionment / reverse charge applicability - evidence requested
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@brightharbor.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: accounts-payable@brightharbor.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2026 15:12:00 +0100
Subject: Marketplace GST treatment and seller apportionment

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving towards onboarding Redwood to manage inference costs across our marketplace of third-party sellers, but we have a couple of tax / invoicing constraints we need to sort before we start routing traffic. Can you confirm the following?

1) If our sellers are non-resident and we (BrightHarbor) are the marketplace operator domiciled in France, does Redwood expect reverse-charge (B2B) treatment on your invoices to us, or do you treat you as providing platform services subject to local VAT?

2) We need a clear apportionment method when a single invoice covers usage for multiple sellers in different EU jurisdictions and different VAT rates (e.g., seller A in IE at 23%, seller B in FR at 20%). Do you provide line-level split invoices, or do you expect us to self-bill / allocate?

3) We'll need to validate the sellers' VAT IDs and provide proof to our tax team. What evidence do you require to release funds held on a payment-hold?

I've attached a CSV of our seller VATIDs and one sample invoice for context. Would appreciate a quick checklist and expected timeline — procurement wants this closed before month-end.

Best,
Emma Li
Head of Marketplace Operations
BrightHarbor Logistics
Mobile: +33 6 12 34 56 78

Attachments: BrightHarbor_VATIDs.csv (CSV), sample-seller-invoice-202603.pdf (PDF)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@brightharbor.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2026 17:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Marketplace GST treatment and seller apportionment

Emma —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Quick answers up front, then a recommended evidence checklist and next steps: 

Short answers:
- For a BrightHarbor account we treat the invoice as B2B platform services. If you provide valid EU VAT IDs for the *buyer* (BrightHarbor) and the underlying sellers, we can apply reverse-charge on Redwood's invoice to BrightHarbor for net VAT reporting. 
- We can produce line-level invoicing if you opt into the marketplace split billing feature (additional configuration). Otherwise our default is a consolidated invoice with metadata per usage line that you can use to self-bill internally.
- To release payment holds we require validated VATIDs + one of: signed reseller agreement or self-billing authorization, plus a sample seller invoice showing billing relationship.

Evidence checklist (what to upload to the Drive link you shared):
1) CSV of seller VATIDs (already provided) — we will validate via VIES and local registries.
2) Copy of your marketplace terms signed with sellers OR a self-billing letter.
3) A sample seller invoice showing how fees are passed through (PDF).
4) Statement of place-of-supply rules you apply (simple doc).

I'll loop in Finance (Sean) to confirm the invoicing option and whether we can emit per-seller line items for March usage retroactively. If you prefer, we can also issue credit notes + reissued split invoices for March once validation completes.

Proposed timeline: VATID validation + evidence review = 3 business days after we receive signed self-billing or reseller manifest. If all OK, payment hold lifted and we issue split invoice within 5 business days.

Next steps: 
- Emma: confirm if BrightHarbor will provide a signed self-billing authorization or you want Redwood to enable split invoices (which requires engineering lead time).
- Sean: will confirm accounting treatment and whether we need a DocuSign credit note for March retroactive splits.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0143
From: Armand Dubois <armand.dubois@brightharbor.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Emma Li <emma.li@brightharbor.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2026 09:27:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Marketplace GST treatment and seller apportionment

Ben / Emma —

We can provide a signed self-billing letter for our sellers (attached). A couple of practical items:

- For a subset of sellers we operate as an intermediary and need the marketplace to mark those line items as 'seller-borne VAT' so our accounting team can offset correctly.
- Some sellers (three in the CSV) are registered outside VIES (non-EU sellers with local tax numbers). We need Redwood to accept manual evidence and let us upload scanned registration certificates for validation.

I've attached the draft self-billing letter. Please confirm which file types you accept for off-VIES evidence (png/pdf).

Thanks,
Armand
Head of Tax & Compliance
BrightHarbor Logistics
Attachments: apportionment-proposal-20260331.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Armand Dubois <armand.dubois@brightharbor.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@brightharbor.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2026 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace GST treatment and seller apportionment

Armand —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the draft. Confirming receipt of your attachments. A few internal notes and the operational path from Redwood Finance: 

- Accepted evidence types for non-VIES sellers: PDF scans of local tax registration, government portal screenshots, or notarized certificates (PDF/PNG/JPG accepted). We'll keep the originals in our compliance portal and flag them on the buyer record.

- For the 'seller-borne VAT' flag: we can add a per-line metadata attribute. If you want the amounts reallocated on our invoice, we need you to opt into split invoicing. Otherwise we'll leave a consolidated net invoice and provide a CSV mapping for your accounts payable to re-allocate.

Marissa — can you confirm whether Finance can accept the signed self-billing letter and release the payment hold once the three off-VIES sellers are validated? Also, confirm if we should prepare credit notes for March usage or process the split as an adjustment in April.

Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Armand Dubois <armand.dubois@brightharbor.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@brightharbor.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace GST treatment and seller apportionment

Hi all —

Thanks for the detail. Finance has reviewed the attachments in the Drive folder. Summary of what we'll do and the gating criteria to release the hold on the March payment: 

1) Required to lift hold: (a) signed self-billing letter covering the March billing period, (b) validated VATIDs for all EU-registered sellers (VIES check + screenshot), (c) scanned local registration docs for non-VIES sellers.

2) Once the above are uploaded and verified by Compliance (target 48 hours), Finance will: 
   - Issue credit notes for March for sellers that need split allocation (so your AP can match amounts).
   - Reissue split invoices (separate line-items) if BrightHarbor enables split invoicing feature; otherwise we will provide a detailed allocation CSV and apply accounting adjustments on Redwood side.

3) Payment timing: If validations finish by EOD Tue 06 Apr, we can lift the hold and process net payment within 5 business days. If validations require manual follow-up on the three off-VIES sellers, that adds up to 7 business days.

4) DocuSign: We prefer the signed self-billing via DocuSign (we'll send a link) to maintain an auditable trail. I'll open a HubSpot ticket and share the DocuSign link to Emma's inbox by Monday.

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/DBL-4982 (invoice record)

If BrightHarbor confirms DocuSign and uploads the three non-VIES docs as PDFs, we'll move forward.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0199
